close_reason: Moot after sgrr.4 dropped the JsContactId newtype (commit 6cf54bc). No type exists to add Display/FromStr/Into impls to; the Id is now bare String which already has those traits intrinsically.
description:
crate-jmap-jscontact-types/src/lib.rs:60-81 defines JsContactId as a transparent
newtype around String with three impls: From<String>, From<&str>, AsRef<str>. It
is missing four conversions that every caller will hit:

- No Display impl. A caller writing format!("ref: {}", id) gets a type error
  and has to write format!("ref: {}", id.as_ref()) — every single call site.
- No FromStr impl. A caller writing "abc".parse::<JsContactId>() does not
  compile. They have to write JsContactId::from("abc"), which also works but
  diverges from the std-trait idiom that all other string-newtypes follow.
- No into_inner or Into<String>. Once a caller has a JsContactId by value and
  wants the owned String back (to feed it to a function taking String), they
  can only do id.as_ref().to_owned() — an extra allocation that the From<String>
  consumed in the first place.
- No Deref<Target=str>. Borrowing as &str works via AsRef but not via Deref,
  so methods like id.starts_with("k") do not autoderef.

Caller-side workaround is trivial each time but the boilerplate is forever and
multiplies across every consuming crate (jmap-contacts-types, jmap-contacts-server,
any third-party JSContact consumer). Comparable workspace newtype JmapId in
jmap-types ships with Display + FromStr per convention; this newtype is the
outlier.

Fix: add the four impls. None is a breaking change.
title: JsContactId lacks Display, FromStr, Into<String> — every caller writes the same boilerplate to extract
